key_insight: Apparent gains in drug-target forecasting may reflect access to future trial evidence rather than genuine prediction.
clinical_relevance: Reliable target prioritisation could inform which hypotheses enter costly clinical trials, but these findings caution against treating model rankings as validated forecasts.
method: Defined each target–disease event as its first clinical trial.
Rebuilt annual biomedical knowledge graphs from 2020 onward.
Evaluated six open language models with and without graph retrieval against a trial-history baseline.
evidence_signal: Evidence available before the decision added at most small gains, while the newest graph clearly improved five of six models but usually included the target–disease pair’s own future trial.
watch_item: Date both inputs and outcomes: using evidence recorded after the decision can leak the answer and inflate forecasting performance.
paper_title: Did the Model Forecast It, or Already Know It? Evaluating Large Language Models for Novel Drug-Target Prioritisation with a Temporal Knowledge-Graph Oracle
